Subject: Kickoff: MAP & POC evaluation plan — MedLytics

Hi Claire / Ian —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, this thread is to kick off the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the MedLytics POC so we have clear owners, success criteria, and a short evaluation plan to hit your July decision timeline. Below is a concise draft we can iterate on in the sync.

High-level POC scope (2–3 weeks):
- Validate retrieval + generation workflow on a subset of clinical knowledge base (de-identified)
- Verify latency & cost under expected QPS
- Measure clinical correctness / hallucination rate on curated eval prompts

Draft success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 300ms for interactive flows (slice: 512 tokens)
- Cost: inference unit cost target <= $0.003/token (configurable via batching/quant profiles)
- Quality: >90% accuracy on clinical QA evaluation set (see attached prompt set)
- Stability: no regression vs baseline on hallucination sentinel tests

Owners (initial):
- MAP lead / customer success: Priya Natarajan (I'll drive the plan, meetings, overall timeline)
- Evaluation & prompts: Dylan Brooks (benchmarks, prompt buckets, run harness)
- Security & data handling: Mina Haddad (privacy, sandbox access, audit logs)
- Commercial / SOW / billing: Marissa Cole

Files attached to start: medlytics_map_v1.xlsx (proposed milestones & timelines), eval_prompt_set.md (seed prompts + labeling rubric).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm stakeholders we should include (I added Jordan for ML infra but add others).
2) Confirm if MedLytics can provide a de-identified sample dataset and whether sandbox access is possible (we can provide an ephemeral private deployment for the POC).
3) Sync — proposed 30-min call: Fri, Jun 19, 10:00 PT. If that works we'll run through the MAP and lock owners.

I'll update the MAP spreadsheet after the call and share HubSpot deal link.

Thanks —

Quick note from the evaluation side — thanks for drafting this, Priya. Proposed concrete lanes for the POC (I'll own coordinating the runs):

1) Latency & throughput lane
   - Synthetic QPS tests + representative prompt sizes (128 / 512 tokens)
   - Measure 95th / p99 and tail behavior with batching enabled/disabled

2) Clinical correctness lane
   - Use the sentinel set Claire mentioned (we'll produce a labeled slice of ~300 QA pairs)
   - Metric: clinically significant error rate (binary) + per-question confidence score

3) Robustness / hallucination lane
   - Hallucination sentinel tests, instruction-following edge cases, and red-team examples

4) Cost & config lane
   - Run same prompts across recommended quant & batching profiles to estimate $ / token and ops cost

I'll drop a short outline in the drive (eval_plan_outline.md) and spin up the harness. If MedLytics can provide the de-id KB to an S3 bucket, we can mirror it into the sandbox for evaluation quickly.

Dylan
